title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry: A Computational Framework for Stability Simulation and Quantum-Enhanced Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework, termed "Dynamic Topological Geometry" (DTG), that leverages the interplay between dynamic topology and quantum entanglement to simulate and optimize complex topological structures. We propose a novel framework for analyzing and manipulating topology, incorporating quantum entanglement to capture the inherent dynamism of topological systems. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional optimization algorithms, particularly in the analysis and control of intricate topological designs. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum entanglement to represent and manipulate the underlying topological dynamics, enabling more precise and efficient optimization of complex structures. This work represents a significant step towards developing advanced computational tools for topology, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Rule Discovery
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for adaptive rule discovery within dynamic systems, leveraging the strengths of neural networks and symbolic programming through reinforcement learning. The core idea is to train a neural network to predict system states and rewards, and then utilize reinforcement learning to optimize a symbolic program that translates these predictions into actionable rules. This iterative process allows for the discovery of complex, adaptive rules without explicit human intervention. The system learns by observing rewards and adjusts the symbolic program, effectively creating a neuro-symbolic engine for rule generation. This approach addresses the limitations of purely data-driven or rule-based systems by combining the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical reasoning capabilities of symbolic programs. The presented framework offers a practical and scalable solution for automating rule discovery in a variety of domains.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation for AI
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint propagation offers a promising approach to accelerate and improve reinforcement learning (RL) training. This paper explores a novel framework, Quantum-Inspired Constraint Generation, designed to dynamically generate constraints based on input data, thereby enhancing the learning process and addressing a critical bottleneck in RL. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary results demonstrating its potential to improve reinforcement learning performance. The core mechanism utilizes quantum-inspired constraints to accelerate learning and offer increased robustness. This work represents a significant step towards leveraging quantum computing to enhance AI training methodologies.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Embodied Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating embodied temporal logic. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both neural networks – their ability to learn complex representations – and symbolic reasoning – its precision and formal guarantees – through a tightly coupled system. We introduce a framework where neural networks represent concepts and relationships, and a temporal logic engine performs reasoning within a temporal context. This allows for robust and verifiable temporal reasoning capabilities, addressing limitations of purely neural or symbolic approaches. The system learns through the neural network, and the temporal logic provides a framework for structured, time-aware deductions. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss its potential applications, focusing on systems requiring reliable temporal understanding and decision-making. The integration of temporal logic provides a crucial layer of formal verification and explanation, enhancing the trustworthiness of the reasoning process.

title: Sector-Mean: Deterministic Initialization of K-Means Centroids via Angular Sector Partitioning
abstract: K-Means is one of the most widely used clustering algorithms, but its susceptibility to initial centroid selection remains a primary bottleneck for its convergence speed and clustering accuracy. This paper proposes Sector-Mean Initialization, a deterministic initialization strategy with O(N) time complexity that partitions the two-dimensional data space into angular sectors around the global centroid and initializes centroids using sector-wise means. We evaluate the method on established two-dimensional benchmarks (SIPU, Birch) and multiple real-world datasets, comparing against random, K-Means++, and Max-Min initialization under identical Lloyd iterations. The statistical analysis of Friedman's test (p<0.05) and Nemenyi post-hoc comparison indicates that, while delivering equivalent clustering quality as K-Means++ and Max-Min, Sector-Mean offers significant computational efficiency. Experimental results show that Sector-Mean reduces the initialization time by 74.9% and 59.8% in comparison to K-Means++ and max-min, respectively. And, it yields the lowest average number of iterations, achieving approximately 5% fewer iterations than K-Means++ and 16% fewer than max-min. These results highlight that Sector-Mean initialization offers a deterministic and computationally efficient initialization strategy while preserving cluster quality.

title: SeaCausal-FL: Federated Fuzzy Causal Learning for Maritime IoT Fault Diagnosis and Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Reliable marine-engine fault diagnosis in maritime IoT is challenged by distributed data ownership, heterogeneous fault distributions, and continuously changing operating conditions. This paper proposes SeaCausal-FL, a federated fuzzy causal learning framework that combines a shared temporal diagnostic path with mechanism-conditioned causal reasoning. An interval type-2 fuzzy layer represents uncertain and overlapping operating mechanisms, while each mechanism is associated with a physics-constrained structural causal model. Before aggregation, locally learned mechanisms are aligned using operating context, causal structure, and conditional intervention-response signatures. Model parameters are then aggregated according to sample, class, mechanism, and mechanism-class evidence instead of client sample size alone. The learned structural equations further support interval counterfactual reasoning through abduction, action, and prediction. Experiments on a marine-engine fault dataset and a real-data-calibrated semi-synthetic causal benchmark show that SeaCausal-FL achieves an average F1 score of 87.07% across four client partitions, with AUROC and AUPRC of 98.98% and 94.81%, respectively. It also maintains strong performance under unseen loads and fault-type omission during training. On the causal benchmark, SeaCausal-FL reaches an Edge-F1 of approximately 0.58 and an Edge-AUPRC of 0.68, reduces coefficient RMSE to about 0.14, and provides favorable counterfactual estimation and intervention decisions.

title: Diagnostics for Subgroup-Coverage Claims in Conformal Prediction
abstract: Group-conditional (Mondrian) conformal predictors are widely reported to improve minority-class coverage over split conformalprediction. We ask whether the usual evidence carries it. Comparing them at a common nominal level conflates conditionaltargeting with conservatism: across seven public clinical tasks the group-conditional predictor over-covers marginally by +0.002to +0.067, so a subgroup difference read at fixed α need not identify any conditional advantage. Fixing realised marginalcoverage removes that confounder and introduces three others, which we measure. Matching on the evaluation sample isan oracle procedure; two of our four estimators are not. Two nulls run identical machinery on predictors that cannot differ,exposing a noise floor that on one dataset exceeds an effect we previously reported and now withdraw. Row-level bootstrappingof clustered patients puts the same patient in training and evaluation folds, inflating the effect with a dose-response in themeasured leak. Of the seven benchmarks, six are not design-resolved under our declared screen, for reasons visible beforeany result is computed. Of three additionally put through leak-free patient-level resampling, one survives. These are separatescreens on different subsets. We recommend reporting such comparisons over a range of coverage targets, with null calibrationand leak-free resampling.

title: Title: Bayesian Hierarchical Diffusion in Vector Spaces
abstract: This paper explores a novel Bayesian hierarchical diffusion process within vector spaces, designed to facilitate the continuous and adaptive creation of complex mathematical functions. Traditional diffusion methods frequently rely on discrete steps, limiting the generation of intricate and nuanced mathematical expressions. We propose a probabilistic algorithm that iteratively refines a function's parameters, guided by Bayesian inference, to achieve this goal. This approach allows for the generation of highly complex mathematical forms, offering potential applications in mathematical proof generation, statistical modeling, and generative art. The core mechanism involves a dynamic parameter adjustment based on observed data, ensuring a smooth and continuous evolution of the mathematical function. This work introduces a new framework for probabilistic function refinement, leveraging Bayesian principles to achieve a more flexible and powerful approach compared to existing techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement via Non-Asymptotic Distribution Arithmetic
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new approach to mathematical geometry computation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and non-asymptotic distribution techniques to achieve precise calculations. This paper proposes a novel method for precisely computing complex geometric structures, potentially providing a new computational paradigm for both quantum computation and specialized geometric problems. We explore the potential of utilizing entanglement to transform the calculation process into a quantum entanglement-based operation, coupled with non-asymptotic distribution methods to guarantee stability and accuracy. This work investigates the feasibility of applying this approach to various geometric transformations and challenges existing computational methods.

title: Quantum Information Search and Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum information search and optimization are crucial for advancing quantum computing and information science. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexity of searching and optimizing quantum states. This paper proposes a novel quantum information search and optimization algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced efficiency in exploring complex quantum states and parameter optimization. We introduce a framework that harnesses the inherent properties of entanglement to facilitate rapid and accurate quantum state traversal, ultimately leading to improved results compared to conventional approaches. The core mechanism centers around the construction of a quantum network that facilitates the exploration of high-dimensional spaces, enabling the efficient identification of optimal quantum states. This research explores the potential of entanglement-based search and optimization techniques to address key challenges in quantum information processing.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration: A Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture based on multi-agent collaboration. The core idea is to construct a network of multiple neural networks, each possessing distinct functionalities and characteristics, and to facilitate collaboration between these agents to achieve enhanced problem-solving capabilities. We introduce a framework where individual agents are tasked with handling specific types of tasks, and a collaborative mechanism is employed to realize the overall objective. This approach leverages the theoretical foundation of multi-agent collaboration to transform neural networks into a multi-agent network, thereby significantly improving their ability to tackle complex problems. The architecture presented here offers a promising direction for developing more robust and adaptable AI systems.

title: 自适应量子算法的并行优化机制
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum algorithm optimization mechanism designed to leverage the unique characteristics of quantum hardware and the inherent parallelism of quantum algorithms. The core concept revolves around a dynamic adjustment of parallel execution based on real-time hardware assessments, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. We present a framework that analyzes quantum circuit parameters and automatically optimizes the parallelization strategy, leading to improved performance. The paper details the proposed mechanism, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements over existing approaches, particularly in scenarios involving complex quantum circuits. The focus is on providing a robust and adaptable approach to quantum algorithm optimization.

title: High-Order Matrix Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Information Storage
abstract: Quantum information storage presents a significant challenge due to the need for precise control and efficient manipulation of quantum states. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to effectively address the complex constraints inherent in this field. This paper proposes a novel high-order matrix optimization algorithm designed to address these challenges, aiming to dramatically improve the efficiency of quantum information storage. The algorithm leverages the inherent properties of high-order matrices to efficiently navigate the space of possible quantum state configurations, offering a pathway towards enhanced storage density and reduced error rates. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated matrix manipulation strategy, coupled with predictive modeling based on calculated efficiency, offering a promising approach to optimizing quantum information storage. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in computational efficiency compared to existing methods, and the resulting predictions offer insights into the potential for enhanced storage capabilities.

abstract: Quantum Information Space Geometry Adaptive Optimization (QISGOA) presents a novel optimization algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum computation to enhance system performance and investigate the geometric structure of quantum information. title: Differential Privacy for Federated Learning via Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging the data itself. However, achieving differential privacy (DP) – a rigorous privacy guarantee – within the FL setting remains a significant challenge due to the computational overhead associated with traditional DP mechanisms. This work introduces a novel approach that combines differential privacy with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to address this limitation. Our method employs a layered SMPC protocol to enable clients to perform gradient updates locally while maintaining privacy. The protocol minimizes data exposure by breaking down the computation into smaller, secure steps. The core claim is that existing DP mechanisms in FL are often computationally expensive. The proposed mechanism combines differential privacy with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to perform gradient updates locally without revealing individual client data, utilizing a layered SMPC protocol for enhanced efficiency. This offers a practical and efficient solution for deploying DP in FL. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that our approach can achieve a desired privacy budget while significantly reducing the computational burden compared to standard DP techniques. This work contributes a new method to improve the performance of DP in FL.

title: Multimodal Causal Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Multimodal Causal Reasoning Engine designed to address the limitations of traditional single-modality causal inference. The core claim is that accurate causal reasoning can be achieved by effectively integrating information across diverse data modalities such as text, images, and video. The engine leverages a hybrid approach combining structured probabilistic graphical models and deep learning techniques to construct a multimodal causal graph and perform reasoning and prediction. Specifically, we utilize a deep learning model to estimate the causal dependencies between different modalities, and then employ a Bayesian network to represent and reason about these dependencies. The engine's ability to handle complex, multi-faceted causal relationships promises to significantly improve prediction accuracy and decision-making in scenarios involving heterogeneous data. The key innovation lies in the automated discovery and representation of causal relationships across modalities, a significant advancement over existing approaches. This work presents a framework for building intelligent systems capable of robust causal inference in complex, real-world environments.

title: 基于概率逻辑的非确定性计算模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational model based on probabilistic logic for simulating stochastic processes and uncertain systems. The model leverages the inference mechanisms inherent in probabilistic logic to represent and reason about randomness, effectively capturing the essence of non-deterministic behavior. The core contribution lies in the integration of probabilistic logic with non-deterministic computation, offering a fresh approach to modeling and analyzing systems where uncertainty plays a significant role. This approach provides a framework for representing probabilities within a logical structure, enabling deductive reasoning about uncertain scenarios. The model is designed to handle situations where outcomes are not definite but instead defined by probabilities. We outline the key components of the model, including the representation of probabilistic propositions and the inference rules used to derive conclusions under uncertainty. The model's ability to simulate stochastic processes and analyze uncertain systems makes it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in various fields, including artificial intelligence, decision-making, and risk management. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions.

title: Probability and Quantum Computing Integration for Quantum Error Correction Algorithm Validation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of integrating probability logic with quantum computing to enhance quantum error correction (QEC) algorithm validation. The core idea is to leverage the inherent randomness of quantum computation to develop a novel framework that optimizes error detection and correction. Traditional QEC methods rely heavily on classical computational resources, limiting their effectiveness in handling intricate quantum states. This work proposes a probabilistic framework, utilizing quantum randomness as a key component, to improve the efficiency and robustness of error detection and correction processes. The investigation focuses on the synergistic combination of probabilistic logic and quantum phenomena to drive improvements in QEC algorithm performance. The study aims to demonstrate a practical approach to validating QEC algorithms using quantum computation, offering a pathway toward more reliable and efficient quantum information processing. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the proposed framework and its potential impact on the field of quantum error correction.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) leveraging reinforcement learning (RL). The core idea is to develop an algorithm capable of dynamically learning and adapting QEC code parameters based on the evolving noise environment. Traditional QEC codes are often pre-defined and may not optimally perform in all scenarios. This research proposes a system where network nodes autonomously adjust the code parameters using an RL framework, reacting to error detection results and feedback signals. The system's ability to self-optimize based on real-time noise characteristics represents a significant advancement in QEC design. The key objective is to enhance error correction performance by adapting to the dynamic nature of quantum noise. The theoretical framework and the proposed algorithm are detailed within this document, highlighting the potential for improved resilience in quantum communication and computation.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Feature Selection in Deep Learning
abstract: This paper investigates feature selection within the context of deep learning, addressing a critical limitation of traditional methods. Traditional feature selection techniques frequently fail to effectively capture the nuanced information content and inherent redundancy present within feature sets. This research proposes a novel approach grounded in information theory, specifically utilizing mutual information and entropy to quantify information gain and redundancy. The core of the methodology involves developing an algorithm designed to maximize information gain while simultaneously mitigating redundancy. The algorithm employs a greedy search strategy, iteratively selecting features based on their mutual information with the target variable, subject to a constraint that penalizes features exhibiting high redundancy with other selected features. The theoretical underpinnings of this approach are rigorously presented, establishing a principled framework for dimensionality reduction in deep learning models. The proposed method demonstrates improved model performance and reduced computational complexity compared to conventional feature selection strategies. Experimental results, though not presented here due to the focus on the theoretical analysis, are anticipated to validate the effectiveness of this information-theoretic feature selection approach.

title: Resource Allocation Based on Physical Models for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for solving complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential necessitates efficient resource allocation within quantum computing systems. Traditional resource allocation approaches often lack a fundamental understanding of the physical constraints inherent in quantum computation, such as decoherence and the limitations of superposition. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum resource allocation that integrates physical models directly into the allocation strategy. We propose a framework where algorithms are designed to balance resource utilization with information fidelity, considering the underlying physics of quantum systems. The core claim is that utilizing physical models for resource allocation can optimize quantum computing performance and efficiency. This work introduces a mechanism based on quantum computing's physical properties – decoherence, superposition – to design resource allocation algorithms, aiming to achieve a better balance between resource utilization and information fidelity. We present a formalization of the resource allocation problem and outline a potential implementation strategy.

title: Quantum Hidden Matrix Dynamics: A Dynamic Adjustment Approach
abstract: Quantum Hidden Matrix (QHM) is a cryptographic technique utilizing a matrix-based security system to ensure the integrity of data. However, traditional QHM implementations often rely on static parameters, limiting their security and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel dynamic adjustment approach to QHM, significantly enhancing both security and computational speed. We propose a method for dynamically adjusting matrix parameters, allowing for a more robust and efficient representation of the quantum system. This dynamic adjustment mechanism, built upon a novel optimization algorithm, allows for the creation of QHM matrices capable of resisting various attacks. The research focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Adaptive Algorithm Selection via Cognitive Network Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates a novel adaptive algorithm selection system leveraging cognitive network analysis to optimize problem-solving. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a "Cognitive Resonance Matrix," a system that dynamically evaluates and weighs various algorithm approaches based on a complex analysis of the problem's characteristics and inherent complexity. The system moves beyond traditional fixed algorithm selection, adopting a dynamic evaluation framework to identify and prioritize the most effective solution path. The research explores the potential of this approach to improve problem-solving efficiency and robustness across a spectrum of challenges. We present a comprehensive evaluation methodology and demonstrate the system's effectiveness through illustrative case studies.

title: Event Interaction in Low-Rank Bottlenecks for Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Temporal relation extraction determines whether an event occurs before, after, or simultaneously with another event, and therefore relies on accurately modeling how the two events interact. Mainstream systems achieve this by concatenating event spans or using shallow fusion, which works well when all model parameters are trainable. However, in parameter-efficient fine-tuning, low-rank bottlenecks restrict information flow and prevent these interaction signals from passing through, leading to clear performance drops. To address this limitation, we propose a theoretically grounded architecture, Convolutional Bottleneck Interaction (CBI), which first applies lightweight depthwise convolution to enhance event representations and then uses element-wise multiplication to capture effective event-event interactions inside the bottleneck. Across five datasets and seven backbone models in the Adapter and LoRA settings, CBI provides consistent and substantial gains, up to +31.7 micro F1, while adding minimal computational cost, showing that explicit interaction inside low-rank spaces is crucial for temporal relation extraction. The code is available at https://github.com/VRCMF/CIF.git.

title: Low-Depth Random Unitaries without Ancillae
abstract: Random unitaries are fundamental to quantum information and many-body physics, with widespread applications ranging from quantum learning and metrology to device benchmarking. A central pursuit is to minimize the space and circuit depth required to generate them. However, existing methods for generating low-depth random unitaries rely heavily on an extensive number of ancillary qubits, imposing severe spatial overhead. In this work, we prove that random unitaries can be generated in optimal depth without ancillae. For multiplicative-error approximate $k$-designs on $n$ qubits, our circuits achieve a depth of $\widetilde{O} (k) (\log n)^{1/δ}$ on $δ$-dimensional architectures and $\widetilde{O}(k) \log \log n$ with all-to-all connectivity. Furthermore, by introducing a general exactification lemma, we lift our construction to optimal-depth exact $k$-designs, yielding an exponential resource reduction over state-of-the-art exact constructions. Our results minimize the space-time costs for a wide range of quantum protocols.

Furthermore, by introducing a general exactification lemma, we lift our construction to optimal-depth exact $k$-designs, yielding an exponential resource reduction over state-of-the-art exact constructions. Our results minimize the space-time costs for a wide range of quantum protocols.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Bayesian Networks (BNs) to model emergent data patterns within complex, distributed systems. The core claim is that this framework offers a significant advancement in data modeling, particularly for systems exhibiting complex, non-linear dynamics. This work presents a theoretical foundation and initial implementation demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential for uncovering hidden patterns and predictive capabilities within intricate data landscapes.

title: Quantum-Inspired Random Walk Algorithms for Graph Search
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-inspired algorithms for graph search problems. Traditional random walk approaches often suffer from inefficiencies, particularly in complex graphs. We propose a novel framework that leverages concepts from quantum walks – specifically interference and tunneling – within a classical computational environment. Our algorithms dynamically adjust the probability distribution of node visits based on graph connectivity and the history of previous steps, mimicking the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics. We demonstrate that this approach can, in certain scenarios, outperform standard random walks, offering a more adaptable and potentially faster search strategy. The core of the method lies in approximating the quantum effects through carefully designed classical simulations, without requiring actual quantum hardware. We present a mathematical formulation of the core algorithm and discuss its key parameters, focusing on the balance between classical simulation fidelity and computational cost. The results suggest a promising direction for graph search optimization, drawing inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics.

abstract: This paper explores the application of simulated annealing (SA) and multi-agent systems (MAS) to address complex optimization problems. The core idea is to leverage the inherent robustness of SA with the collaborative potential of MAS. Each agent independently employs the SA algorithm to explore the solution space, while a defined collaboration mechanism facilitates information exchange, competition, and cooperation among the agents. This synergistic approach aims to enhance the search process and ultimately converge toward a global optimum. We present a framework for designing and implementing such a system, outlining key components and collaboration strategies. Through this methodology, we aim to demonstrate the effectiveness of combining these two powerful techniques for tackling challenging optimization problems.

title: Temporal Relational Graph Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel learning algorithm, Temporal Relational Graph Learning (TRGL), designed to effectively capture and leverage relational structure within dynamic graphs, explicitly incorporating temporal dependencies. TRGL addresses the limitations of existing approaches by employing a "relational memory" module – a recurrent neural network integrated with a differentiable relational tensor – to dynamically update and refine relationship representations based on observed temporal changes. The core mechanism utilizes a recurrent network to process the graph's evolving state, while the relational tensor allows for the representation and modification of relationships. We demonstrate that this approach moves beyond static graph embeddings and traditional temporal graph networks by directly modeling the evolution of relationships and their interdependencies, resulting in a more robust representation of dynamic systems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining its potential for applications in areas such as social network analysis, anomaly detection, and dynamic systems modeling.

title: Optimizing ASTER and PRISMA data for lithological mapping and mineral detection in NW Pakistan
abstract: Remote sensing is a fundamental tool in mineral exploration and lithological mapping. The northern mountainous belt of Pakistan has significant mineral deposits, although hyperspectral data remain underutilized in this region. This study applied an integrated techniques, including principal component analysis (PCA), independent component analysis (ICA), minimum noise fraction (MNF), spectral angle mapper (SAM), mahalanobis distance (MD), spectral index (SI) and support vector machine (SVM) to ASTER and PRISMA data for mapping lithological units and alteration zones in the Garam Chashma region of northwest Pakistan. These approaches successfully isolated target signals, delineated lithological units and mineralization zones, and demonstrated a strong spatial correlation with ground observations and known Cu-Fe mineralization. Field validations and laboratory analysis confirm the remote sensing results and additional identified potential areas near Garam Chashma town, including Momi village, along Arkari Gol and west of the Drunil area. The results supports the reliability of the adopted methodology for minerals exploration globally.

title: A Bayesian-optimized CNN-GRU framework for multimodal short-term solar photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: The integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into the energy grid presents several challenges for controlling energy systems, primarily due to their intermittent nature. To manage this intermittency, accurate short-term forecasts are required. This study proposes a Bayesian-optimized sequence-aligned hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) framework to predict PV power 15 min ahead using multimodal sky images ( 6 4 × 6 4 × 4 8 ) and historical PV time-series data (16 × 1). Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) optimization with Hyperband pruning is employed to systematically search the hyperparameter space. On a standardized 1-year benchmark dataset, the proposed model achieves an overall Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2 . 4 1 9 k W , a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1 . 1 5 3 k W , and a Forecast Skill (FS) of 18.96%. These results demonstrate a 3.36% improvement in RMSE, a 7.83% improvement in MAE, and a 17.40% relative improvement in Forecast Skill compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) model, while achieving an 80.0% reduction in model parameters.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Curves in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the integration of adaptive complexity curves within evolutionary algorithms to enhance robustness and mitigate premature convergence. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with local optima, necessitating careful parameter tuning and potentially lengthy search times. We propose a novel mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search space based on a 'complexity curve' – a visual representation of the system's internal state and observed patterns – allowing the algorithm to intelligently navigate complex landscapes. This approach aims to promote greater exploration and ultimately lead to more effective solutions. The core of our design lies in monitoring the system's internal state and adjusting the search space to avoid getting trapped in suboptimal regions of the search space. We present a theoretical framework for the complexity curve and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of simulations focusing on a specific optimization problem.

title: FADE-RIPE: A Robust Quantum Optimal Control Algorithm for Superconducting Transmons with Realistic Hardware Constraints (reference implementation)
abstract: FADE-RIPE: Transmon Quantum-Gate Optimizer FADE-RIPE (Fidelity Aware, Distortion-aware, Environment-conscious Robust Iterative Pulse Engineering) is a gradient-based quantum optimal control method for a single-qubit gate on a 4-level (N=4) transmon, benchmarked against GRAPE and CRAB (via qutip_qtrl). The model and optimizer include: Realistic transmon physics: An N=4 Hilbert space with Kerr/anharmonic H0, a subspace-projected 2x2 target gate, and an explicit penalty for population leaking into levels |2>, |3>. Exact Lindbladian propagation and gradient: Piecewise-constant Lindblad master-equation propagation with an exact analytic gradient (via the augmented-generator/Frechet-derivative trick). AWG bandwidth filter: A Butterworth low-pass filter on the control pulses, represented as an exact linear operator so the gradient chain rule through it is exact. Filter-function noise penalty: A numerical filter function F(omega) of the optimized pulse, penalized against a 1/f (flux) or thermal-photon power spectral density via an overlap integral. Thermal initial-state fidelity: As-built fidelity optimizations starting from a Boltzmann-weighted thermal state rather than the pure ground state. This upload contains the reference implementation fade_realistic.py, which includes the physics model, optimizer, baseline comparisons, and the analysis/plotting pipeline used for the simulations reported in the companion paper.

title: Title: Self-Assembling Topological Networks for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-assembling topological networks to data compression, offering a novel approach that leverages the inherent structure of topological spaces to achieve efficient data representation. Traditional compression methods often require complex algorithms and significant computational resources. This work proposes a fundamentally different strategy: dynamically adjusting the connectivity of a network based on the data's characteristics, effectively creating a self-organizing structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential for improved compression rates and reduced computational overhead compared to conventional methods. The core of our design involves the creation of a topology that adapts to the data, leading to a more robust and adaptable compression technique.

title: ##拓扑映射的自适应量子纠缠生成
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information, is crucial for secure communication and powerful quantum computation. Traditional methods of generating entanglement often rely on complex, pre-defined protocols. This paper proposes a novel quantum entanglement generation algorithm based on the robust and adaptable properties of topological mappings. We develop a system that dynamically adjusts the mapping parameters to generate entangled states tailored to the evolving quantum state. The core mechanism leverages the inherent topological structure of mappings to create entanglement without requiring explicit manipulation of the underlying quantum states. This approach offers a promising pathway towards efficient and adaptable quantum entanglement generation, potentially revolutionizing quantum communication and computation. We detail the algorithm's architecture, key mathematical formulations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) presents a revolutionary paradigm shift in the field of artificial intelligence, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance machine learning algorithms. title: Title: Universal Prime Number Generation via Quantum Simulation (UPQGS)
abstract: The generation of prime numbers has historically relied on deterministic algorithms, limiting their security against brute-force attacks. This paper introduces Universal Prime Number Generation via Quantum Simulation (UPQGS), a novel quantum algorithm designed to produce prime numbers with a guaranteed level of randomness and enhanced security. We propose a quantum simulation approach that leverages the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to explore the prime number space in a statistically diverse manner. The core mechanism centers on utilizing a quantum algorithm to simulate the evolution of a prime number generator, generating a statistically representative set of prime numbers. This approach promises to provide a fundamentally new method for cryptographic security, surpassing the limitations of traditional prime number generation techniques. The research will detail the quantum algorithm, its implementation, and the resulting characteristics of the generated prime numbers, emphasizing the algorithm's ability to achieve a high degree of randomness and statistical diversity.

title: ##基于多变量因果推断的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of quantum algorithms by leveraging the principles of causal inference. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on heuristic methods or black-box approaches, lacking the transparency and robustness required for complex systems. We propose a novel framework that integrates causal inference with quantum algorithm design, aiming to identify and mitigate critical factors influencing algorithm performance. The core of our approach involves constructing a causal model of the quantum algorithm, represented as a causal Bayesian network. This network allows us to explicitly model dependencies between algorithmic components, enabling targeted interventions to improve efficiency and accuracy. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis, outlining a methodology for identifying confounding variables and implementing causal interventions. The resulting framework offers a more interpretable and reliable path towards optimizing quantum algorithms, particularly in scenarios where understanding underlying causal relationships is paramount.

title: Quantum Algorithm Optimization Based on the Many-Worlds Interpretation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization by leveraging the Many-Worlds Interpretation (MWI) of quantum mechanics. The core idea is that MWI's concept of parallel universes can be exploited to accelerate quantum computation through probabilistic superposition across multiple universes. We propose a quantum algorithm design where the algorithm operates in a superposition of universes, enabling intermittent interactions and enhanced search efficiency. The algorithm utilizes the inherent probabilistic nature of MWI to explore a vast computational space concurrently, potentially overcoming limitations faced by standard quantum algorithms. This research introduces a new paradigm for quantum algorithm optimization, moving beyond traditional methods by embracing the multi-universal perspective. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and algorithmic design, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of quantum optimization processes. Further research will focus on developing specific implementations and evaluating the algorithm's performance against established quantum optimization techniques. ---

title: LLM-Extracted Temporal Hypergraphs for Modeling Disease Severity and Clinical Trajectories From Clinical Documents (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Clinical trajectory modeling requires representations of how multiple clinical dimensions interact and evolve over time. Conventional knowledge graphs are limited to pairwise edges and therefore cannot natively represent the higher-order interactions that characterize clinical events, in which patient factors, findings, treatments, and severity co-occur. No integrated framework combines large language model (LLM)-driven structured extraction from unstructured clinical documents with temporal hypergraph construction for trajectory modeling. OBJECTIVE We aimed to develop and validate a four-dimensional (4D) temporal hypergraph framework (4D-HyperGraph) that unifies patient history, clinical evidence, treatment trajectory, and dynamic severity in a single representation for clinical trajectory modeling. METHODS Four-dimensional clinical information was extracted from eight types of unstructured Chinese clinical documents for a retrospective cohort of 251 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD; stable, n=54; acute exacerbation, n=88; exacerbation with infection, n=109), using a two-stage deidentification pipeline and LLM-driven extraction with dimension-specific prompts. Hyperedges were typed by dimension and assembled into a temporal hypergraph with HyperGraphRAG. A hypergraph neural network (HyperGNN) with dimension-level and temporal attention was trained for three-way classification, exacerbation prediction, and severity regression against a clinical severity composite score (CSCS). Five baselines were compared under stratified 5-fold cross-validation across 3 seeds, with dimension-level ablation, a temporally disjoint hold-out split, and external validation at a second hospital. RESULTS For three-way classification, 4D-HyperGraph with an XGBoost readout (4D-XGB) reached a 3-seed mean macro-averaged F1 of 0.615 (SD 0.010; 95% CI 0.580–0.653) versus 0.427 (SD 0.008) for the structured-feature XGBoost baseline, and 0.550 (SD 0.012) versus 0.436 (SD 0.017) on the temporally disjoint split. Exacerbation prediction reached a 3-seed mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.711 (SD 0.013) internally but 0.695 (SD 0.015) on the temporal split, below the structured baseline (0.715, SD 0.009). Externally, a balanced cohort (n=87) yielded an AUC-ROC of 0.865 versus 0.822 for the baseline, whereas external three-way classification stayed below baseline (macro-F1 0.449 vs 0.484; 0.441 vs 0.467 in a label-quality sensitivity analysis). For severity regression, the end-to-end HyperGNN achieved R2=0.216 and Pearson r=0.575, the highest among the deep-learning architectures; removing the severity dimension produced the largest ablation effect (r declined by 20.7%). No comparison survived Bonferroni correction (5 baselines × 3 tasks; corrected α=.003); the differences are indicative rather than confirmatory. CONCLUSIONS 4D-HyperGraph provides a general approach—designed to be disease-agnostic—for constructing temporal hypergraphs from unstructured clinical documents. Its primary contribution is at the representation level: the 4D encoding captures multi-way clinical relationships that improved classification and supported severity prediction in this proof-of-concept study. Transfer to an independent hospital was most robust for exacerbation risk, whereas fine-grained three-way classification remained affected by cross-source distribution shift and infection-label boundary noise. Multicenter, multidisease validation is the necessary next step.

title: Detokenization Leaks: Reconstructing Local LLM Outputs From Cache Traces
abstract: We present a new attack that reconstructs the text generated by locally hosted LLMs by observing CPU cache activity during detokenization. Unlike prior attacks that rely on deployment-specific assumptions, such as shared data memory, CPU offloading, or Mixture-of-Experts architectures, our approach targets the detokenizer, a component used in default LLM inference pipelines. To obtain clean signals, we use Flush+Reload on shared tokenizer code to detect when decoding occurs, which lets us perform Prime+Probe at the right moment and isolate token-dependent cache activity. We then apply a clustering-and-language-model pipeline to recover text from noisy cache observations. We evaluate the attack across multiple datasets, hardware platforms, inference frameworks, and model families, and show that it can recover semantically accurate outputs from real-world local LLM deployments, including agentic systems. This vulnerability is particularly significant because the most widely used tokenizer implementations are susceptible to the attack and are embedded in many popular local LLM products and agent frameworks, including systems such as OpenClaw (which we demonstrate), substantially broadening the practical attack surface.

evidence.title: Detokenization Leaks: Reconstructing Local LLM Outputs From Cache Traces
evidence.abstract: We present a new attack that reconstructs the text generated by locally hosted LLMs by observing CPU cache activity during detokenization. title: Title: Probabilistic Logic Programming with Dynamic Contextualization
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic logic programming framework designed to enhance reasoning capabilities in systems dealing with uncertainty and dynamic environments. Standard logic programming techniques often struggle with incomplete information, requiring significant manual intervention. We introduce a dynamic contextualization mechanism that updates the program's internal state based on observed data, incorporating a model of the surrounding context. This allows the system to reason more effectively about uncertainty and adapt to changing conditions, addressing limitations of current approaches and offering a promising path towards more robust and flexible logical reasoning. The core of our design is a probabilistic system that iteratively refines the program's internal representation, incorporating observed data and a dynamically updated model of the context. We explore a specific implementation utilizing a Bayesian updating approach to model the contextual shift, demonstrating its potential for improved performance in complex scenarios.

title: Title: Adaptive Neural Network Activation Function Design
abstract: This paper explores the design of an adaptive neural network activation function that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the inherent non-linearity of input data. The core challenge in traditional neural networks is their inability to effectively model complex, non-linear relationships within the data, limiting their expressive power. This work proposes a novel activation function architecture that incorporates a self-adjusting parameter system, allowing the network to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input and improve model performance. We introduce a mechanism for dynamically modifying the activation function's parameters, thereby enabling the network to better represent and learn from the data's underlying structure. The resulting activation function demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness in a range of neural network tasks, particularly when dealing with data exhibiting significant non-linearity. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement in neural network design, addressing a critical limitation in many applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement's Dynamic Matrix Reconstruction Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computational paradigms. This paper explores a novel dynamic matrix reconstruction algorithm predicated on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance computational accuracy and stability. The core mechanism leverages entanglement to create a feedback loop, iteratively refining the matrix reconstruction until a desired level of precision is achieved. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum computing. title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Geometric Expansion
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational science, leveraging quantum mechanics to unlock new possibilities across diverse fields. This paper explores the development of a novel geometric expansion technique, utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to dramatically enhance the capabilities of quantum computation. We propose a framework where geometric calculations are intrinsically linked to quantum algorithms, allowing for the simulation of complex geometric structures and quantum systems with unprecedented efficiency. The core claim is that this geometric expansion can overcome the limitations of classical computation, opening avenues for advanced modeling and analysis in areas like materials science, drug discovery, and fundamental physics. This work details the underlying mechanisms, explores the potential applications, and provides a preliminary assessment of the technological feasibility of this approach.

title: Dynamic Neuron Connection Weight-Dependent Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic neuron connection weights in adaptive learning systems. The central claim is that neuron connection weights are not static but rather adapt dynamically based on internal neuron states and environmental changes. This dynamic adjustment is proposed as a core mechanism to improve learning efficiency. The research challenges the traditional assumption of static connection weights in neural networks by exploring the impact of dynamic weights on learning performance. A model is designed incorporating feedback mechanisms and adaptive algorithms to facilitate this dynamic weight adjustment. The investigation aims to provide a theoretical framework and demonstrate the advantages of a dynamic approach to learning compared to conventional static weight models. The key mathematical formulation explores the relationship between neuron state, environmental input, and the updated connection weights. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of neural network learning and suggests a novel pathway for designing more efficient and robust adaptive learning systems.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Optimization via Game Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of game theory optimization techniques to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments. The core claim centers around leveraging the optimization methodologies inherent in game theory to enhance the collaborative efficiency and overall performance of multi-agent systems. The primary mechanism involves constructing a MARL environment and employing game-theoretic mechanism design principles to refine agent strategies and communication protocols. Specifically, we explore how techniques from cooperative game theory, such as Nash equilibrium analysis and Shapley value calculations, can be integrated into the learning process within a multi-agent setting. This approach directly addresses the inherent challenges of MARL, particularly the issues of strategy conflict and resource competition among agents. The research demonstrates a potential pathway for improved coordination and decision-making in complex multi-agent scenarios. The theoretical framework presented provides a novel approach to MARL optimization, offering a structured methodology for designing and implementing efficient multi-agent systems.

title: Adaptive Data Augmentation for Deep Learning in Low-Data Regimes
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success across various domains, largely due to the availability of large datasets. However, obtaining such extensive datasets is often a significant challenge, particularly in specialized fields or scenarios where data acquisition is expensive or time-consuming. In these low-data regimes, traditional data augmentation techniques frequently prove ineffective, often exacerbating model overfitting rather than improving generalization. This paper introduces an adaptive data augmentation strategy designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to create a feedback loop wherein the augmentation process dynamically adjusts based on the model's current state, prioritizing regions of high uncertainty. We formulate this approach using a Bayesian neural network framework, allowing for the quantification and targeted amplification of data in areas where the model's predictive confidence is weakest. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance compared to static augmentation techniques in low-data settings, showcasing the potential of adaptive augmentation for boosting deep learning model robustness and accuracy when data is scarce.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Adaptive Rule Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to artificial intelligence—Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Adaptive Rule Generation—designed to overcome limitations inherent in traditional rule-based systems and deep learning models. The core idea is to combine the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the representational and reasoning power of symbolic programming. This synergy allows for the dynamic generation and refinement of symbolic rules directly from raw data, leading to more adaptable, explainable, and efficient intelligent systems. The system operates through a closed-loop mechanism: a neural network identifies salient patterns within data, and a symbolic engine then constructs and iteratively improves rules based on these patterns. This adaptive process addresses the challenge of brittle rule sets in traditional systems and the lack of interpretability in deep learning. The paper outlines the architecture of the system, details the adaptive rule generation process, and discusses the potential applications and future research directions.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection with Relational Reasoning
abstract: Anomaly detection in graph data presents unique challenges due to the inherent complexity of relationships between nodes. Existing methods often rely on isolated node features or simple graph metrics, failing to adequately capture the intricate dependencies that define anomalous behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph anomaly detection that leverages graph embedding techniques coupled with relational reasoning algorithms. The core idea is to learn rich representations of graph structures and their relationships, and then identify deviations from expected patterns using rule-based systems or other relational reasoning methods. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves anomaly detection accuracy compared to traditional methods by explicitly modeling and analyzing the relational context of graph nodes and edges. The system is designed to detect anomalies by identifying nodes or edges that exhibit unusual relational patterns. The proposed methodology offers a more nuanced and effective strategy for detecting graph anomalies, particularly in scenarios where relationships are crucial to understanding normal and abnormal behavior.

abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology algorithm based on quantum spin dynamics. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum spin parameters, allowing for more efficient parameter tuning and improved algorithm performance. The algorithm leverages the inherent properties of quantum spin to iteratively refine the system's state, leading to enhanced results. The core mechanism involves a self-consistent update loop that modifies the spin states based on a predefined objective function. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on parameter optimization, potentially yielding superior outcomes compared to conventional methods. We detail the algorithm's design, theoretical analysis, and preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a specific quantum optimization problem.

title: Neuromorphic Computing for Procedural Content Generation
abstract: Procedural content generation (PCG) has become a cornerstone of modern game development and creative design, offering automated methods for producing vast and diverse content. However, conventional PCG algorithms often rely on computationally intensive techniques like Monte Carlo simulations or complex rule-based systems, leading to performance bottlenecks and limitations in generating truly novel and complex structures. This paper proposes a novel approach to PCG utilizing neuromorphic computing, specifically employing Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). SNNs, inspired by the biological brain, offer inherent parallel processing capabilities and energy efficiency, making them ideally suited for real-time content generation. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of mapping PCG algorithms onto SNNs, focusing on the translation of iterative processes into spiking events. The core claim is that leveraging the inherent parallelism of SNNs allows for the creation of significantly more complex and varied content compared to traditional methods. We present a framework for designing SNNs for specific PCG tasks, including level generation, landscape modeling, and architectural design. The potential for achieving unprecedented levels of realism and complexity in content generation is highlighted, demonstrating a shift in paradigm for creative algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this emerging field, including the optimization of SNN architectures and the development of novel PCG algorithms specifically tailored for neuromorphic hardware.

title: Ads from automatons: Consumer perceptions of AI modality disclosures and the roles of AI experience and dispositional persuasion knowledge on advertising outcomes
abstract: Extant literature on consumer reactions to AI-generated advertising have focused on resulting perceptions of creativity, objectivity, and effectiveness in specific situations, often invoking situational persuasion knowledge as a framework to guide explanations of reactions. Though informative, this leaves a research gap with regard to other forms of persuasion knowledge, ad contexts, and advertising-relevant outcomes. Through an experimental approach and in response to platform-specific guidelines and proposed laws mandating disclosures of AI-generated content in advertising, the current study seeks to understand the interaction of dispositional persuasion knowledge, experience with AI tools, and trust in AI to better explain consumer reactions to online banner ad elements labeled as generated by AI. We find a general consumer ambivalence toward advertising disclosed as AI-generated vs. a non-AI-generated control (regardless of AI-generated modality), but also novel positive effects of dispositional persuasion knowledge, AI experience, and trust in AI with regard to specific advertising-focused dependent variables when the use of AI-generated text in ads is disclosed. Theoretical and practical takeaways for marketers are discussed.

title: A Ticket from Marginals to Joints: Coupled-Noise Distillation for One-Step Block Generation in Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Can a diffusion language model generate a coherent token block in one forward pass? Masked models already predict every position at once, but each prediction is the marginal distribution given the visible context, so the tokens can be mutually inconsistent and later steps revise those already committed. We introduce CONDOR (Coupled-Noise Distillation for One-Step Readout), trained from scratch to map different noise samples to different coherent blocks. Initially, random noise is not naturally paired with a target. TinyStories experiments show diverse, coherent continuations over successive blocks, one forward pass each. Qualitative MNIST experiments show that the same approach can extend to multimodal generation, such as text-to-image and unconditional text-and-image generation.

The core of the innovation lies in the utilization of self-organizing topology, which facilitates the network's ability to learn effectively from complex, unstructured data. title: Algorithmic Self-Repair in Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for achieving algorithmic self-repair in adaptive neural networks. Traditional adaptive neural networks often struggle with catastrophic forgetting – the tendency to lose previously learned knowledge when trained on new data. This paper introduces a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism, termed the "Error-Correction Loop," that proactively analyzes network output and automatically adjusts weights to mitigate errors and enhance performance. The core mechanism centers around a real-time error analysis and iterative weight refinement, addressing a significant challenge in continual learning and boosting the robustness of these networks. We detail the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and potential implications for machine learning systems.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity to manipulate the fundamental fabric of reality. title: Title: Modular Quantum State Collapse (MQSC)
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible transition from a superposition of states to a single, definite state. Traditional approaches to quantum computation often involve a single, global collapse, which presents significant challenges in terms of scalability and error correction. This paper introduces Modular Quantum State Collapse (MQSC), a novel framework for efficiently collapsing multiple quantum states simultaneously. MQSC leverages a set of modular operations designed to selectively collapse multiple parts of a system, dramatically reducing the computational burden inherent in conventional approaches. We propose a new methodology for managing and manipulating quantum states, offering a fundamentally different perspective on quantum computation. This paper details the design of these modular operations, explores their impact on computational complexity, and discusses potential applications of MQSC in various quantum computing paradigms. The core claim of this research is that MQSC provides a significantly more efficient and scalable approach to quantum state manipulation, paving the way for advancements in quantum information processing.

The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the clustering quality and adjusts the parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and experimental results, showcasing its ability to outperform existing methods in terms of cluster quality and efficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Coding and Decoding Framework (QICF)
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum Entanglement Information Coding and Decoding Framework (QICF), a novel approach to quantum information processing designed to overcome the limitations of classical communication channels and mitigate information loss. The core claim of QICF is the utilization of multi-body quantum entanglement to achieve information encoding and decoding rates surpassing those attainable through classical channels. The framework is predicated on a mechanism involving precisely controlled generation and measurement of entanglement within a superconducting qubit array. We leverage the quantum coherence inherent in entangled states for efficient information encoding and decoding, complemented by a robust error correction protocol. Unlike traditional single-qubit-based quantum coding schemes, QICF's utilization of multi-body entanglement offers significant advantages in terms of encoding efficiency and error resilience. This work details the theoretical underpinnings of QICF, outlining the key components and operational principles. We propose a framework for implementing QICF using current superconducting qubit technology, acknowledging the challenges and potential improvements. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the feasibility of achieving reliable quantum communication and information processing through the exploitation of entangled quantum states.

title: Probabilistic Graphical Models Based on Spatial Data Structures
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing the efficiency of probabilistic graphical model inference by leveraging spatial data structures. Traditional probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) often struggle with scalability when dealing with large spatial datasets, leading to computationally expensive inference processes. This research proposes a framework that integrates PGMs with spatial indexing structures, such as k-d trees and R-trees, to significantly accelerate inference speed. The core idea is to utilize the spatial locality inherent in the data to reduce the search space for nodes during probabilistic reasoning. The proposed method offers a practical solution for modeling and reasoning about spatial data, opening up opportunities for applications in areas like environmental modeling, urban planning, and anomaly detection. This paper details the theoretical foundations, the proposed integration mechanism, and discusses the potential performance gains compared to traditional approaches.

title: Temporal Anomaly Detection via Phase-Space Reconstruction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to temporal anomaly detection by leveraging the principles of phase-space reconstruction. The core idea centers on mapping a time series data into a high-dimensional phase space, reconstructing this space using manifold learning techniques, and then identifying anomalies as deviations from the expected manifold structure. The paper details the methodology, outlining the key steps involved in the reconstruction process and the criteria used for anomaly identification. We demonstrate the applicability of this approach through a theoretical framework, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional anomaly detection methods. The primary focus is on the mathematical underpinnings and the conceptual framework, providing a foundational understanding for future research and implementation. The proposed technique aims to provide a systematic approach to analyzing temporal data and uncovering hidden patterns indicative of anomalous behavior.

title: Algorithmic Bias Detection in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources, preserving data privacy. However, the inherent data heterogeneity across clients introduces a significant challenge: algorithmic bias. This paper presents a novel method for detecting and quantifying bias within the federated learning process. Our approach leverages statistical measures and differential privacy techniques to monitor model updates and identify bias amplification. We define key metrics such as variance of model updates, divergence between client models, and the sensitivity of model predictions to sensitive attributes. The core of our method is the adaptive adjustment of learning rates based on these metrics, aiming to mitigate bias while maintaining model convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential for robust and fair FL systems. The proposed framework provides a quantifiable assessment of bias risk and suggests strategies for bias mitigation during the training process.

title: CogSent: Cognition-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Through Fast–Slow Thinking
abstract: Sentiment analysis of multimodal social media data is of great importance, not only for recognizing objective information but also for capturing subjective emotional states. While single-modal sentiment analysis has achieved notable progress, existing multimodal approaches still face two key challenges: (1) inadequate modeling of subjective emotional characteristics and (2) insufficient handling of cross-modal inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we propose an image-text multimodal sentiment analysis framework (CogSent) grounded in the psychological Dual-System Theory. First, inspired by human fast and slow thinking, we develop a Hierarchical Dual-Channel Cognition (HDCC) architecture to extract intuitive and rational affective features, respectively. Second, we introduce an Intuition-Guided Cognition Refinement (IGCR) module that uses System-I-inspired intuitive representations as affective priors to retrieve and refine System-II-inspired contextual representations via cross-attention. Third, we propose a Dynamic Cross-Modal Cognition Fusion (DC2F) network that predicts sample-adaptive thresholds from modality discrepancy, agreement, and attention statistics, dynamically regulating directional image–text interaction to mitigate interference from conflicting cross-modal sentiment signals. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that CogSent achieves improved performance compared to existing methods and yields competitive results on multiple evaluation settings.

title: Power Mean Estimation in Stochastic Continuous Monte Carlo Tree Search
abstract: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) has demonstrated success in online planning for deterministic environments, yet significant challenges remain in adapting it to stochastic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), particularly in continuous state-action spaces. Existing methods, such as HOOT, which combines MCTS with the Hierarchical Optimistic Optimization (HOO) bandit strategy, address continuous spaces but rely on a logarithmic exploration bonus that lacks theoretical guarantees in non-stationary, stochastic settings. Recent advancements, such as POLY-HOOT, introduced a polynomial bonus term to achieve convergence in deterministic MDPs, though a similar theory for stochastic MDPs remains undeveloped. In this paper, we propose a novel MCTS algorithm, \Algname, designed for continuous, stochastic MDPs. \Algname integrates a power mean as a value backup operator, alongside a polynomial exploration bonus to address the non-stationarity inherent in continuous action spaces. Our theoretical analysis establishes that \Algname converges at a polynomial rate of $\mathcal{O}(n^{-ζ})$, $ζ\in (0,1/2)$, where \( n \) is the number of visited trajectories, thereby extending the non-asymptotic convergence guarantees of POLY-HOOT to stochastic environments. Experimental results on stochastic tasks validate our theoretical findings, demonstrating the effectiveness of \Algname in continuous, stochastic domains.

evidence.title: Power Mean Estimation in Stochastic Continuous Monte Carlo Tree Search
evidence.abstract: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) has demonstrated success in online planning for deterministic environments, yet significant challenges remain in adapting it to stochastic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), particularly in continuous state-action spaces. Existing methods, such as HOOT, which combines MCTS with the Hierarchical Optimistic Optimization (HOO) bandit strategy, address continuous spaces but rely on a logarithmic exploration bonus that lacks theoretical guarantees in non-stationary, stochastic settings. Recent advancements, such as POLY-HOOT, introduced a polynomial bonus term to achieve convergence in deterministic MDPs, though a similar theory for stochastic MDPs remains undeveloped. In this paper, we propose a novel MCTS algorithm, \Algname, designed for continuous, stochastic MDPs. \Algname integrates a power mean as a value backup operator, alongside a polynomial exploration bonus to address the non-stationarity inherent in continuous action spaces. Our theoretical analysis establishes that \Algname converges at a polynomial rate of $\mathcal{O}(n^{-ζ})$, $ζ\in (0,1/2)$, where \( n \) is the number of visited trajectories, thereby extending the non-asymptotic convergence guarantees of POLY-HOOT to stochastic environments. Experimental results on stochastic tasks validate our theoretical findings, demonstrating the effectiveness of \Algname in continuous, stochastic domains.

title: El ocaso del espejismo de la IA Agéntica: análisis crítico de costos ocultos, vulnerabilidades de inyección de prompts e inmunidad de infraestructura en sistemas corporativos. Un enfoque desde la experiencia de la Ingeniería de Datos y la seguridad de redes
abstract: El presente artículo analiza la viabilidad económica, operativa y de seguridad de la integración de agentes de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) autónomos en sistemas de Planificación de Recursos Empresariales (ERP) y Gestión de Relaciones con Clientes (CRM). Frente a la narrativa comercial que postula el reemplazo total del modelo de Software como Servicio (SaaS), este documento expone la fragilidad estructural del enfoque agéntico basado en APIs de terceros debido al denominado “impuesto del token” y a los bucles recurrentes de retroalimentación (prompt looping). Adicionalmente, se desmitifica la simplicidad de la implementación de Modelos de Lenguaje Pequeños (SLMs) en entornos locales, detallando la deuda técnica y las restricciones asociadas a la cuantización y la orquestación. Desde la perspectiva de la ciberseguridad, se evalúa el riesgo sistémico de la adopción de plataformas como OpenClaw dentro de clústeres corporativos, considerando la viabilidad de ataques por inyección malintencionada de prompts, escapes de contenedor y movimientos laterales en redes puente. Finalmente, se propone un modelo de inmunidad digital fundamentado en una arquitectura asíncrona estrictamente desvinculada de la red (airgapped) y una política de Confianza Cero basada en validación humana mediante comandos de privilegios altos controlados asociados a claves temporales encriptadas generadas desde autenticadores criptográficos físicos.

title: unused-assumptions: theorems in Mathlib whose stated setting exceeds what their proof requires
abstract: A mechanical search over Mathlib for theorems whose stated algebraic setting is stronger than their own proof needs: replace one instance binder with a weaker class, keep the proof unchanged, compile it alone. Published with the data and a verifier that recompiles every row.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Morphological Networks – Pattern Recognition Through Emergent Structure
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-organizing network architecture designed for pattern recognition, specifically focusing on the automatic construction and evolution of morphological patterns within data. Recognizing the limitations of traditional machine learning approaches, which often require extensive manual feature engineering, we introduce the "Dynamic Morphological Re-ordering" algorithm as the core mechanism for generating complex and adaptable patterns. This algorithm iteratively refines the network's structure based on local feedback, fostering emergent behavior and allowing for the discovery of intricate patterns without explicit design. We detail the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying and classifying diverse patterns. The paper explores the potential applications of this architecture across various pattern recognition tasks, highlighting its ability to automatically generate robust and adaptable morphological representations.
